title: Extract filterByName helper from Go APIItems handler and test it directly
description: The Go web app APIItems handler contains inline name-filter logic. Extract it into a named, testable helper function.

task_spec.prompt:
The APIItems handler in internal/handler/items.go filters items inline when ?q= is set. Refactor it:

1. Extract the filter logic into:
   func filterByName(items []Item, q string) []Item
   - q is already lowercased before the call (or normalize inside the function — your choice)
   - Returns items whose Name contains q (case-insensitive)
   - Returns all items if q is empty
   - Returns a non-nil empty slice (not nil) when nothing matches

2. Update APIItems to call filterByName instead of inline logic.

3. Write 3 unit tests for filterByName directly:
   TestFilterByName_Match — q="widget" matches "Widget A"
   TestFilterByName_NoMatch — q="xyz" returns empty slice (len == 0)
   TestFilterByName_EmptyQuery — q="" returns all 3 items

The refactor must not change any observable behaviour. All 3 existing tests (TestIndex, TestAPIItems, TestAPIItemsFilter) must still pass. go test ./... and go build ./... must succeed.
required_artifacts: func filterByName(items []Item, q string) []Item in items.go
success_criteria: filterByName is a public or package-level function callable from tests
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `go test ./...` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
